name: near
description: NEAR Protocol as one mod. NEAR's personality is its account model: accounts are human-readable names (alice.near) or 64-hex implicit accounts, an account and a contract are the same object, and access keys carry per-contract permissions — session auth on chain. This module reads all of it (balances with staked and storage-locked NEAR priced in USD, access keys, contract methods parsed from the deployed WASM export section, view calls, NEP-141 tokens, history, transactions, validators) and now writes all of it: a keystore under ~/.mod/near/, contract deploys with a batched init call (redeploying upgrades in place), signed change calls with gas and deposit, transfers, account creation (testnet faucet mints funded *.testnet names; elsewhere sub-accounts of the signer), access-key management. Writes default to testnet; a non-testnet write refuses without confirm=true; a write over HTTP needs the token from ~/.mod/near/token. ed25519 via PyNaCl with a pure-Python RFC 8032 fallback, borsh in-tree — still zero hard dependencies. A curated directory of the contracts that are ON — well-known contracts per network plus anything deployed from the keystore — is re-verified live against the chain. And a census the chain itself cannot be asked for: a scraper tails every new block's state changes to catch each contract deploy as it lands, backfills history backwards through the archival RPC, and folds in every lookup that finds code — a local, self-sustaining index of every contract on the network, no third-party indexer, resuming across restarts. Semantic search over that census runs locally too: tf-idf over account ids, curated labels and parsed WASM method names, a concept lexicon so "stablecoin" finds USDt and "lending" finds Burrow, trigrams so typos still land — no model, no external service. Twenty-one MCP tools, a REST API and a browser console run the same code on one port.

endpoints.call_change: POST /call {contract, method, args?, gas_tgas?, deposit_near?, token}

backend: python stdlib only (http.server + urllib); WASM export-section parser, borsh serializer and RFC 8032 ed25519 in-tree (PyNaCl used when present)
auth: reads open; writes sign with keys from ~/.mod/near/ (never the repo) — non-testnet writes refuse without confirm=true, HTTP writes need the token from ~/.mod/near/token, secret keys never leave the keystore

env.PORT: port for API, console and MCP (default 50910)
env.NEAR_RPC: your own RPC endpoint — skips the public failover pool
env.NEAR_OFFLINE: skip the tests that need the chain
env.NEAR_SCRAPE: 0 turns the contract scraper's threads off (the stored index still answers)
env.NEAR_TAIL_POLL: seconds between chain-head checks for the live tail (default 6)
env.NEAR_SCAN_RPS: archival requests per second the history backfill spends (default 1)
env.NEAR_SEARCH_TTL: seconds the search index is reused before rebuilding from the store (default 60)
